content: The Abbott RealTime MTB and MTB RIF/INH platforms are advanced diagnostic tools designed for the detection of Mycobacterium tuberculosis complex (MTBC) and resistance to rifampicin (RIF) and isoniazid (INH). These platforms utilize real-time polymerase chain reaction (PCR) technology to amplify and detect specific DNA targets associated with tuberculosis (TB) and drug resistance. Sample Preparation and Inactivation Sputum samples can undergo optional decontamination or liquefaction before being treated with an inactivation reagent for one hour. For the RealTime MTB assay, DNA extraction is not required, and the process takes approximately five hours. The same sample preparation steps apply to the MTB RIF/INH assay. Reagent Preparation and DNA Amplification Reagents and reaction plates can be prepared either manually or using the automated m2000sp instrument. The prepared samples are then loaded onto the m2000rt instrument for real-time PCR, fluorescence detection, and automated reporting. This process takes about two hours. Detection of Drug Resistance The MTB RIF/INH assay identifies mutations in the rpoB gene (for rifampicin resistance), katG gene, and inhA promoter region (for isoniazid resistance). Results are categorized as negative, detected, indeterminate, or undetected based on the detection of wild-type and mutant probes. Specific mutations associated with lowor high-level INH resistance are also reported. Equipment and Reagents The Abbott RealTime MTB and MTB RIF/INH assays require specific reagent kits, including amplification reagents, internal controls, and positive/negative controls. The m2000sp and m2000rt instruments are essential for automated sample preparation and real-time PCR. Proper storage conditions for reagents include temperatures between -15°C and -25°C, with opened packs used within specified timeframes (14 days for MTB reagents and 90 days for RIF/INH reagents). Operational Considerations The testing capacity of the RealTime MTB assay is 96 samples per kit, while the MTB RIF/INH assay processes 24 samples per kit. Maintenance of the m2000 system includes daily, weekly, and monthly servicing, with annual maintenance provided by the manufacturer. Connectivity options allow data export to laboratory information systems, although manual export via CD-ROM is required due to the lack of USB connectivity. Training and Quality Assurance Training for the Abbott m2000 system is more complex than other TB testing platforms, requiring at least five days of theoretical and practical instruction. BD MAX MDR-TB Test The BD MAX MDR-TB test is another nucleic acid amplification test (NAAT) for detecting MTBC and resistance to RIF and INH. It targets specific genomic elements (IS6110, IS1081, and katG) and is performed on the BD MAX platform, which automates DNA extraction and real-time PCR. Results are available within four hours and include detection of MTBC, RIF resistance, and INH resistance. Roche cobas MTB and MTB-RIF/INH Assays The Roche cobas MTB and MTB-RIF/INH assays detect MTBC and drug resistance using the cobas 6800/8800 systems. These tests target the 16S rRNA and esx genes for MTBC detection and the rpoB, katG, and inhA regions for drug resistance. The cobas systems are capable of high-throughput testing, processing up to 1,056 tests per 8-hour workday. WHO Recommendations The World Health Organization (WHO) recommends moderate-complexity automated NAATs, such as the Abbott, BD MAX, and Roche platforms, for detecting pulmonary TB and drug resistance in respiratory samples. These tests are preferred over culture and phenotypic drug susceptibility testing due to their diagnostic accuracy and faster turnaround times. Implementation Considerations Countries should prioritize placing these systems in national or regional reference laboratories with adequate infrastructure and sample volumes. The multi-disease testing capabilities of these platforms can optimize resource use and reduce costs across disease programs. Conclusion The Abbott RealTime, BD MAX, and Roche cobas platforms represent significant advancements in TB diagnostics, offering rapid and reliable detection of MTBC and drug resistance. Their integration into national TB programs can enhance diagnostic capacity and support global efforts to combat TB and drug-resistant TB.
